title: Monitoring plan and accountable owner
core: A post-deployment monitoring plan covering the system exists.
objective: Each deployed predictive AI system has an approved post-deployment monitoring plan that names an accountable owner and sets the measures, cadence, thresholds, escalation path, and remediation authority, with monitoring intensity tiered by risk.
activity: Approve the plan before go-live; review it at least annually and after every material model update, threshold breach, or incident.
evidence: Approved monitoring plan with version history; responsibility (RACI) matrix; review minutes.
cadence: Before go-live; annually; on material change.
owner_role: System owner, approved by the AI governance body or equivalent

title: AI system and model inventory
core: Deployed AI systems are recorded in an inventory.
objective: An inventory lists every deployed predictive AI system with its version, developer, task and output type, deployment sites, data inputs, monitoring plan, and a link to or copy of the current source-attribute record.
activity: Update the inventory at deployment, update, and retirement; reconcile it against EHR configuration at least quarterly.
evidence: Inventory export with change log; quarterly reconciliation record.
cadence: On change; quarterly reconciliation.

title: Developer monitoring obligations in contracts
core: Contracts with the developer require notice of security incidents and vulnerabilities.
objective: Contracts with the intervention developer require notice, within contract-defined time frames, of model updates, changes to known risks, new validation results, security incidents, and vulnerabilities, and delivery of updated source attributes.
activity: Include notice clauses and time frames in contracts; track developer notices and confirm source attributes are refreshed after each notice.
evidence: Contract clauses; developer notice log; source-attribute refresh records.
cadence: At contracting and renewal; on each developer notice.

title: AI incident response integration
core: The incident response plan addresses AI-specific incidents.
objective: Incident response plans cover AI-specific incidents (performance collapse, harmful or biased outputs, misuse, compromise of model or data), with severity criteria, containment steps, internal and external communication, and reporting, and are exercised at least annually.
activity: Add AI scenarios to the incident response plan and run at least one AI scenario in the annual exercise.
evidence: Incident response plan with AI annex; exercise after-action report.
cadence: Annual exercise; plan update after each AI incident.
owner_role: Incident response lead with the system owner

title: External sharing of monitoring findings
core: A defined policy governs sharing monitoring findings outside the organization.
objective: Monitoring findings (incidents, drift, bias, security issues, outcome evaluations) are shared with the developer and, under a defined policy and subject to legal and privacy review, with peer deployers and sector bodies such as information sharing and analysis centers or patient safety organizations.
activity: Apply a sharing policy that sets what is shared, with whom, how fast, and with what de-identification.
evidence: Sharing policy; log of findings shared and recipients.
cadence: On each qualifying finding; policy reviewed annually.

title: Monitoring resources and competence
core: Monitoring has a budget, and monitoring staff and users are trained for the system.
objective: Monitoring has budgeted resources (outcome labels, compute, reviewer and clinician time, tooling), trained staff, and users trained on the intervention's intended use and limits.
activity: Set the monitoring budget in the plan; train monitoring staff and users before access and when the intervention changes.
evidence: Budget line; training records; staffing assignments.
cadence: Annual budget; training at onboarding and on change.

title: Independent assessment of monitoring
core: Someone independent of the build/operate team periodically assesses the monitoring.
objective: An assessor independent of the team that built or operates the system periodically reviews monitoring design, metrics, thresholds, and results, and findings are tracked to closure.
activity: Schedule independent review by risk tier (for example, annually for high-risk systems); track findings in a risk register.
evidence: Independent review report; findings tracker.
cadence: By risk tier; at least every two years.

title: Performance baseline and deviation thresholds
core: A pre-deployment local baseline with deviation thresholds is recorded.
objective: Before go-live, the organization records the baseline the system will be monitored against (validity metrics with uncertainty from the developer's internal and external validation results and, where feasible, from a local silent trial) and sets deviation thresholds that trigger review, correction, or deactivation.
activity: Run a local silent (shadow) trial where feasible; record baseline metrics and confidence intervals; set thresholds in the monitoring plan.
evidence: Baseline report; threshold table in the monitoring plan.
cadence: Before go-live; after every model update.
owner_role: Clinical or business owner with the data science lead

title: Local validity monitoring
core: Validity is measured in the deploying organization's own data.
objective: The intervention's validity in local data (for example discrimination, calibration, and positive predictive value at the operating threshold) is measured with confidence intervals at the planned cadence and compared with the baseline and thresholds.
activity: Compute validity metrics on each monitoring window; flag threshold breaches to the owner.
evidence: Monitoring dashboard extracts; threshold breach log.
cadence: As set in the plan (for example monthly or quarterly), plus event-driven.

title: Input data and population drift detection
core: Input data and population mix are compared against a reference distribution.
objective: The distribution of input features, missingness, upstream data changes (for example code-set or EHR build changes), and the patient-population mix are monitored against the training-data description and the baseline, with alerts on meaningful shift.
activity: Run drift statistics on each monitoring window; review alerts with data owners; record upstream changes.
evidence: Drift report; upstream change log; alert review notes.
cadence: Weekly or monthly automated; on upstream change.
owner_role: Data engineering with the data science lead

title: Outcome label acquisition
core: Reference-standard outcome labels are obtained for monitored cases.
objective: The organization defines how and when reference-standard outcomes are obtained for monitored cases (source, label definition, expected delay, adjudication sample) and uses label-efficient or proxy measures, with stated uncertainty, while labels are delayed.
activity: Write a label specification; adjudicate a sample of labels; report proxy measures with their limits until labels mature.
evidence: Label specification; adjudication agreement statistics; proxy-measure notes.
cadence: Defined before go-live; adjudication sample each monitoring cycle.
owner_role: Clinical owner with the data science lead

title: Longitudinal record and version comparison
core: Performance results from earlier points in time remain available for comparison.
objective: Monitoring results are kept as a time series across model versions and configuration changes, and every update is compared against the current version on the same local data before it goes live where the organization controls update timing, and otherwise promptly after.
activity: Keep results in a versioned store; run a champion-challenger or before-and-after comparison for each update.
evidence: Longitudinal results store; version comparison reports.
cadence: Continuous retention; each update.

title: Correction and deactivation triggers
core: A mechanism with assigned authority exists to supersede, disengage, or deactivate the system.
objective: Threshold breaches lead to pre-defined actions (review, recalibration or retraining request, restricted use, or deactivation) with a named authority, time limits, and user notification; reactivation requires a new baseline.
activity: Write a trigger-action table; record each breach, the action taken, and its timing.
evidence: Trigger-action table; breach and action log; deactivation and reactivation records.
cadence: On each breach.

title: Subgroup performance baseline
core: Subgroup performance is evaluated before deployment.
objective: Before go-live, validity by subgroup is recorded for the characteristics listed in 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(iv)(A)(5)-(13) (a list the regulation gives for evidence-based interventions, used here as a reference set) that are used as inputs or available locally, from developer and local silent-trial results, and subgroup disparity thresholds are set.
activity: Compute subgroup metrics in the silent trial; compare them with developer-reported fairness; set disparity thresholds in the plan.
evidence: Subgroup baseline report; disparity threshold table.
cadence: Before go-live; after every model update.
owner_role: Data science lead with the health equity lead

title: Local fairness monitoring
core: Fairness of the intervention is measured in the deploying organization's own data (subgroup performance and output disparities).
objective: Subgroup validity and disparity in local data are measured at the planned cadence, and disparities beyond thresholds are investigated.
activity: Compute subgroup metrics on each monitoring window; investigate and document breaches.
evidence: Subgroup monitoring report; investigation notes.
cadence: As set in the plan, aligned with GM-FUN-02.
owner_role: Data science lead with the health equity lead

title: Central, tamper-protected monitoring logs
core: Administrative and security logs of the AI system's components that the organization operates go to the organization's central, access-protected log store, with an alert if logging stops.
objective: Inference events, inputs or their hashes (minimized for protected health information), outputs, model version, user actions, and monitoring results are logged to a central, access-controlled, tamper-evident store with risk-based retention, and an alert fires when logging stops.
activity: Route AI system logs to the central log platform; test the logging-failure alert.
evidence: Log pipeline configuration; retention setting; logging-failure alert test.
cadence: Continuous; alert test quarterly.

title: Service level and cost telemetry
core: Service levels and indirect costs of the AI system are tracked.
objective: Availability, latency, error and timeout rates, fallback use, and direct and indirect costs (compute, licensing, labeling, reviewer and clinician time, energy) are tracked per intervention.
activity: Report service levels against targets; report cost per intervention each budget cycle.
evidence: Service-level report; cost report.
cadence: Continuous service levels; quarterly cost.

title: Change and configuration control for AI components
core: Changes the organization makes to AI models and configuration pass through change control.
objective: Model versions, thresholds, input mappings, and EHR build changes pass through change management with pre-change testing, a rollback plan, and an update to the monitoring baseline and the organization's source-attribute record.
activity: Require a change ticket for every AI configuration change; block closure until baseline and attributes are updated.
evidence: Change tickets; rollback plans; attribute update records.
cadence: On each change.
owner_role: Change advisory board with the system owner

title: Fallback and recovery
core: AI artifacts and configuration are backed up and restorable; a fallback workflow exists.
objective: A documented fallback workflow runs when the intervention is unavailable or deactivated, and model artifacts and configurations are backed up and restorable to a known-good version.
activity: Document the fallback workflow; back up artifacts and configuration; test restore at least annually.
evidence: Fallback procedure; backup records; restore test report.
cadence: Annual restore test; procedure reviewed with each update.
owner_role: Platform engineering with the clinical owner

title: User feedback capture and adjudication
core: End users can report problems with outputs, and the reports are integrated into monitoring metrics.
objective: Users can flag outputs in the workflow (wrong, unhelpful, harmful) with little effort; feedback is triaged, adjudicated, fed into metrics, and the outcome is reported back.
activity: Provide in-workflow feedback; triage weekly; include adjudicated feedback in monitoring reports.
evidence: Feedback log with adjudication outcomes; monitoring report section on feedback.
cadence: Continuous capture; weekly triage.

title: Interaction and override telemetry
core: User interactions with outputs are measured.
objective: How users act on outputs is measured (alert or display rates, acceptance, override and dismissal with reasons, time to action, alert-fatigue indicators), aggregated by user role and site.
activity: Report interaction metrics each monitoring cycle; review shifts in reliance or override patterns.
evidence: Interaction telemetry report.
cadence: Each monitoring cycle.
owner_role: Clinical informatics with the data science lead

title: Source-attribute currency and user transparency
core: The deploying organization updates the source-attribute record when an underlying fact changes.
objective: The plain-language source-attribute record available to users is reviewed on a schedule and whenever monitoring changes a value, and each attribute carries a last-reviewed date and an evidence pointer. Missing information is handled by attribute: for the 11 attributes listed in 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(v)(A)(2), information that is not available is shown as not available rather than left blank; for the other 20 attributes, (v)(A)(1) expects complete and up-to-date descriptions, so a missing or outdated value is recorded as a gap and raised with the developer, not marked not available.
activity: Hold an attribute register with review dates; update it from monitoring outputs, developer notices, and change tickets; track gaps in the 20 attributes without a not-available allowance until the developer resolves them.
evidence: Attribute register with review dates and evidence links; user-facing attribute display.
cadence: At least annually per attribute; within 30 days of any change in a monitored value.
owner_role: Clinical informatics with the system owner

title: Adversarial input, misuse, and anomalous behavior detection
core: AI-specific anomalous or adversarial behavior is detected.
objective: Anomalous or crafted inputs, out-of-distribution queries, unexpected output distributions, and behavior that differs between test and production conditions are detected and routed to security operations.
activity: Run input and output anomaly rules; compare production behavior with evaluation behavior; route alerts to the security operations queue.
evidence: Detection rules; alert log; triage records.
cadence: Continuous.
owner_role: Security operations with the data science lead

title: Vulnerability management for AI components
core: AI software components the organization operates are in its vulnerability management program.
objective: Vulnerabilities in model-serving software and libraries (including those on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog), weaknesses in model artifacts, and AI-specific weaknesses are tracked and remediated by risk, and the developer is required to disclose them.
activity: Include AI components in vulnerability scanning and patching; track AI weaknesses in the vulnerability register.
evidence: Scan results; remediation records; vulnerability register entries.
cadence: Continuous scanning; remediation by severity.

title: Access control over models, configuration, and monitoring data
core: Access to AI configuration and monitoring data follows least privilege.
objective: Only identified roles can change model configuration, thresholds, the organization's source-attribute record, or monitoring results; privileged access is separate and MFA-protected; access is reviewed and revoked promptly.
activity: Enforce role-based access; review access quarterly; monitor failed logins to AI administration endpoints.
evidence: Access control lists; access review records; login monitoring alerts.
cadence: Quarterly review; continuous login monitoring.

title: Privacy-preserving handling of monitoring data
core: Monitoring data are handled with privacy protections.
objective: Monitoring data are minimized, de-identified where feasible, encrypted in transit and at rest, and retention-limited, and the privacy impact of monitoring (including telemetry about users) is assessed.
activity: Assess privacy impact of the monitoring design; apply minimization and encryption; enforce retention limits.
evidence: Privacy impact assessment; data handling configuration; retention enforcement records.
cadence: Before go-live; on change to monitoring data.

title: Requirements register for the deployed system
core: Applicable AI legal and regulatory requirements are documented.
objective: A register lists the legal, regulatory, certification, and contractual obligations that apply to the deployed AI system and the monitoring evidence that meets each, and is reviewed when requirements change.
activity: Maintain the register; review it at least annually and on regulatory change; link each obligation to GAP-M evidence.
evidence: Requirements register with evidence links.
cadence: Annual; on regulatory change.

title: Source-attribute completeness audit
core: Each source attribute is periodically checked for population, currency, evidence, or a not-available indication.
objective: Each predictive-DSI source attribute is periodically audited to confirm it is populated, within its review interval, backed by evidence, or, where the regulation allows, explicitly shown as not available.
activity: Sample the attribute register; check population, review date, and evidence; log and fix discrepancies.
evidence: Audit worksheet; discrepancy log.
cadence: Annually, before accreditation reviews, and after developer certification updates.

title: Out-of-scope and policy-violating use monitoring
core: Use of the system is checked against its documented intended scope.
objective: Use outside the intended use, population, users, or setting, use against cautioned uses (for example on excluded populations, or as a replacement for clinical judgment), and violations of terms of use are monitored, reported, and corrected.
activity: Run rules that flag use outside the documented boundaries; review flags each monitoring cycle.
evidence: Out-of-scope use rules; flag review log; corrective actions.
cadence: Each monitoring cycle.

title: AI incident and near-miss log with impact fields
core: AI incidents and errors are recorded.
objective: AI-related incidents and near misses are logged with patient-, population-, and equity-impact fields (affected subgroup, severity, scale, reversibility) so diffuse and cumulative harms can be aggregated.
activity: Add AI impact fields to the safety event system; aggregate quarterly.
evidence: Incident and near-miss log; quarterly aggregate review.
cadence: Continuous logging; quarterly aggregation.
owner_role: Patient safety with the AI governance office

title: Outcome and benefit measurement
core: Benefit measures are defined and tracked.
objective: The intended benefit (outcome, process, or experience measures) and unintended downstream effects are tracked at population level, with periodic review of whether benefits are realized and references to evaluations kept.
activity: Define benefit measures before go-live; review realized benefit and side effects at least annually.
evidence: Benefit measure definitions; annual benefit review; evaluation references.
cadence: Annual review.

title: Affected-community engagement and appeals
core: Patients and affected communities have a route to report problems and appeal outcomes, fed into metrics.
objective: Patients and affected communities can report problems and appeal AI-influenced outcomes, are engaged periodically on impacts, and their input is integrated into monitoring metrics.
activity: Publish a reporting and appeal route; hold periodic engagement; include results in monitoring reports.
evidence: Appeal route; appeal log; engagement summaries.
cadence: Continuous route; engagement at least annually.
owner_role: Patient experience with the AI governance office
